History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
50-year-old woman with 5–6-day history of persistent dry cough, runny nose, chills, myalgias, and fatigue—most consistent with an uncomplicated viral upper respiratory infection.

History:
• Onset & course: Cough and rhinorrhea began ~5–6 days ago; symptoms persistent but not worsening.  
• Cough: Dry, continuous, interferes with sleep; no sputum, no hemoptysis, no chest pain.  
• Upper-airway symptoms: Runny nose; mild throat irritation attributed to coughing; no significant odynophagia; no ear pain/discharge or blockage.  
• Constitutional: Feels cold/shivery, lethargic, generalized myalgias (arms, legs); subjective fever but temperature not measured.  
• Respiratory: Denies daytime dyspnea; no wheeze; breathless only during coughing episodes.  
• GI: Brief diarrhea at illness onset, resolved; no nausea/vomiting; appetite preserved.  
• GU: Normal micturition.  
• Skin/musculoskeletal: No rashes; muscle soreness noted.  
• Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no persistent diarrhea, no urinary symptoms, no rash.  

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – reportedly well-controlled on medication.  
• Hypertension – on medication, self-monitored.  

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with partner (partner well).  
• Occupation: IT developer; largely sedentary job; missed 1 workday due to illness.  
• Tobacco: Former smoker, quit 6 months ago.  
• Alcohol: Wine 2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings/week; counselled to reduce.  
• Illicit drugs: Not mentioned.  

Family History:
• Father – Type 2 diabetes.  
• Otherwise non-contributory.

Physical Examination:
Vitals: Not recorded.  
General / HEENT / Chest / CVS / Abdomen / Neuro / Skin: Not recorded (telephone consultation).

Investigations:
• None performed or ordered during this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
Most likely uncomplicated viral upper respiratory infection; influenza also possible given chills and myalgias.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Viral upper respiratory infection – dry cough, rhinorrhea, duration <1 week; no focal chest signs.  
2. Influenza – chills and diffuse myalgias support; absence of documented fever opposes but does not exclude.  

Issue 1: Acute viral respiratory illness  
Assessment: Likely viral URI vs. influenza; currently uncomplicated.  
Plan:  
• Symptomatic care: rest, adequate oral fluids, regular paracetamol (dose not specified).  
• Off-work advice: take 1–2 additional rest days; reassess fitness for work next week.  
• Education: typical course 7–10 days.  
• Safety-net: return sooner (within 2–3 days) if cough worsens, fevers develop/ persist, breathing becomes difficult, or no improvement; possible in-person evaluation and consideration of antibiotics if secondary bacterial infection suspected.

Issue 2: Chronic conditions (Type 2 diabetes, hypertension)  
Assessment: Reportedly stable; no acute concerns raised.  
Plan:  
• Continue current Metformin and Lisinopril.  
• Reinforce importance of routine follow-up with primary care/diabetes clinic.  
• Lifestyle: reduce alcohol intake (target ≤2 glasses/week initially, taper further); maintain smoking cessation.

Issue 3: Health maintenance / Prevention  
Plan:  
• Encourage annual influenza vaccination (not discussed but routine for T2DM patients) – consider at next visit.  
• Consider pneumococcal vaccination per guidelines.

General plan items: none additional.

Quality checks:
• Vitals and physical exam findings absent (telephone visit).  
• Medication doses, routes, frequencies not documented.  
• No documented allergies to confirm (patient denies).  
• No objective temperature recorded despite chills.  
• Transcript clear; no conflicts with DDx identified.
